intro: You're looking for a remortgage and want to find the best option near you. Whether your current deal is ending, you want a better rate, or you need to borrow more, a mortgage broker can help you compare deals and understand the costs. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK mortgage broker who will quote you directly, with no obligation.
need_heading: What people searching for a remortgage usually need
need_lead: Most people searching for the best remortgage mortgage near me are looking for clear, local help to compare remortgage options and avoid costly mistakes.
needs: Your current fixed-rate deal is coming to an end and you want to avoid moving onto your lender's standard variable rate.
You want to borrow more against your home, perhaps for home improvements or to consolidate other debts, and need to know if remortgaging is suitable.
You're considering changing your mortgage term, maybe to reduce monthly payments or to pay off your mortgage sooner.
You've seen a better rate advertised but aren't sure whether the total cost, including fees, makes it worth switching.
You want to check whether your current lender offers a better deal before looking elsewhere, as a remortgage can be with your existing lender or a new one.
context: When you search for the best remortgage, it's worth remembering that 'best' depends on your circumstances. A broker should compare total costs, not just interest rates, including any arrangement fees, valuation fees and legal costs. Some lenders offer free legal work or free valuations, which can affect the overall cost. Also check whether your current mortgage has early repayment charges that would apply if you switch before your deal ends.

Searching 'near me' suggests you may prefer a local broker you can meet or speak to on the phone. Mortgage advice is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), so any broker or adviser you use should be authorised, or be an appointed representative of an authorised firm, and you can check this on the FCA register. Brokers must tell you whether they search the whole of the market or a limited panel of lenders, and how they are paid, whether by lender commission, a fee, or both.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when enquiring
tell: The value of your property and the amount you still owe on your current mortgage.
Your current mortgage lender, the type of deal you're on, and when your current deal ends.
Whether you want to borrow more money and, if so, how much and for what purpose.
Any early repayment charges that apply to your current mortgage, if you know them.
Your preferred contact method and whether you'd like a broker who works locally or is happy to advise by phone.
Any particular requirements you have, such as a broker who searches the whole of the market or one who has experience with your situation.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the mortgage broker
questions: Do you search the whole of the market or a limited panel of lenders?
How are you paid for your service, and will I receive a clear breakdown of any fees?
Will you compare the total cost of remortgaging, including arrangement fees, valuation fees and legal costs?
Can you check whether my current lender offers a better deal before looking at other lenders?
What early repayment charges might apply if I switch now, and how can I find out?
Are you authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, and what qualifications do you hold?

faqs.q: How do I know if a remortgage is right for me?
faqs.a: A remortgage replaces your current mortgage with a new deal, either with your lender or a new one, to change rate, term or borrowing. It may be right if your current deal is ending, you want a better rate, or you need to borrow more. A broker can help you compare the costs and decide.

faqs.q: What should I check before remortgaging?
faqs.a: Check for early repayment charges on your current mortgage, as these can be significant. Also compare total costs, not just rates, including arrangement fees, valuation fees and legal costs. Some lenders offer free legal work, which can reduce the overall cost.

faqs.q: Will a remortgage affect my credit score?
faqs.a: A remortgage involves a credit check, which may temporarily affect your credit score. However, if you keep up with payments, it can help build your credit history over time. It's a good idea to avoid making multiple applications in a short period.

faqs.q: Can I remortgage with my current lender?
faqs.a: Yes, you can remortgage with your current lender, often called a product transfer. This can be simpler and may avoid some fees, but it's still worth comparing other deals to make sure it's competitive. A broker can check both options for you.

extra_heading: Why a remortgage broker can help you weigh up the 'best' deal
extra: Searching for the best remortgage near you often means you have a rough idea of what you want but aren't sure how the figures stack up once fees, legal work and your current deal's exit charges are added in. A broker can lay the options side by side so you can see the total cost of each, rather than being drawn to the lowest headline rate alone.

It's easy to assume that the deal with the smallest interest rate is always the cheapest, or that staying with your current lender is simplest. Neither is automatically true: a slightly higher rate with free legal work and no arrangement fee can work out better, and your existing lender's product transfer may or may not be competitive. A broker can check both the product transfer route and the wider market where they have access to it.

At a first conversation, expect to talk through your current mortgage, when your deal ends, what you owe and what you want to achieve. The broker should explain whether they search the whole of the market or a limited panel, how they are paid, and what early repayment charges might apply before you commit to anything.

extra_faqs.q: Is a product transfer the same as a remortgage?
extra_faqs.a: A product transfer is when you take a new deal with your existing lender, and it can be quicker and involve less paperwork. A remortgage more broadly means replacing your current mortgage with a new deal, which could be with your lender or a different one. A broker can compare both routes for you.

extra_faqs.q: Do I need to wait until my current deal ends to start looking?
extra_faqs.a: No, it's sensible to start exploring options before your deal ends so you understand any early repayment charges and can time a switch. Lenders and brokers often work to their own timescales, so ask the broker what's realistic for your situation. Starting early gives you room to compare without feeling rushed.
